review.alternative: Preferences may form entirely through immediate reward signals without requiring structured episodic recall.
review.would_change_mind: Observation that agents without episodic recall mechanisms develop identical stable preference trajectories under stochastic environments.

claims.statement: Episodic memory recall provides temporal credit assignment structures that stabilize preference formation in sequential decision tasks.

support.explanation: Demonstrates that modeling temporal credit assignment across episodic sequences is critical for reinforcement learning dynamics.

review.alternative: Internal narratives are post-hoc rationalizations rather than functional drivers of preference trajectories.
review.would_change_mind: Empirical data showing that disrupting narrative recall has zero measurable impact on long-term behavioral consistency.

claims.statement: Human and artificial memory systems rely on structured internal stories or biographies that shape perceived identity and functional choices over time.

support.explanation: Highlights the foundational role of memory and internal life stories in shaping human identity and continuous behavior.
support.passage: In many ways, our memories shape who we are. They make up our internal biographies - the stories we tell ourselves about what we've done with our lives.
